long_biography.plain_text:
An expensive mistake in a college dealership's service department pushed David W. Wilson toward sales: he needed the commissions to repay the damaged engine. The role suited him. After graduating from the University of Northern Iowa in 1970, he advanced through dealership management in Iowa and Phoenix before taking a minority interest in Toyota of Orange in 1983.

Wilson bought the dealership outright two years later and used it as the foundation for Wilson Automotive Group. The business expanded across California, Arizona, Nevada and Mexico, combining Toyota and Honda stores with Ford, Acura and Mazda franchises. Wilson's operating model has emphasized promotion from within, employee retention and customer loyalty. He remains the group's chairman and chief executive.

Wilson bought the dealership outright two years later and used it as the foundation for Wilson Automotive Group. The business expanded across California, Arizona, Nevada and Mexico, combining Toyota and Honda stores with Ford, Acura and Mazda franchises. Wilson's operating model has emphasized promotion from within, employee retention and customer loyalty. He remains the group's chairman and chief executive.
